text:
leo: Quick sync: started int8 onboarding for 'kestrel-lite' on staging with streaming enabled. Replay harness (5k req) shows structured-output parse failures clustered at concurrency >=12. ~1.3% overall.

tanya: any examples? trailing commas or mid-token truncation?

leo: small excerpt pasted below. looks like partial tokens and interleaved KV prefixes when micro-batches coalesce. Request id rcp-9901.

leo: ```
2026-03-21T09:41:12Z WARN parse_json: Unexpected end of input
model=kestrel-lite kernel=int8-opt
req=rcp-9901 qps=120 concurrency=16
raw_stream_preview="{"op": "search", "args": ["foo",  "bar"

--token-chunk--"
```

sam: that raw_stream_preview looks like the stream split between batch boundaries. Could be tokenizer output boundary shifting under int8 kernels. Were these websocket streaming requests or plain HTTP chunking?

leo: streaming websockets. The HTTP runner replay doesn't reproduce it, only our websocket runner under load.

runtime-bot: experiment 1730000042 deployed by sam: toggled batching.window=16 -> 8 for kestrel-lite canary. status=ok

leo: retested with batching.window=8: failures halved to ~0.6%. interestingly, if we disable kv_prefix_sharing the failures go to 0.05%.

tanya: hypothesis: prefix_coalescing merges partial token buffers from different requests when kernel emits boundary token slightly earlier/later due to quant error. For int8 paths this could change token emission timing.

sam: plan suggestion: 1) add token-level interleaving fuzz harness (drive N parallel streams and randomly split tokens across micro-batches), 2) run kernel compare int8 vs fp16 to capture emission timing deltas, 3) add a lightweight parser repair that attempts one reparse after appending common closers ("]}", "]").

leo: implemented (1) quick harness in testkit and pushed to staging runner. attaching small log of a failing case.

leo: ```
[stream] s1: "{"action": "lookup", "ids": [101,"
[stream] s2: "23, 45]"
[merged] result: {"action": "lookup", "ids": [101,23, 45]"
```

tanya: interesting: merged result shows tokens from s1 and s2 fused. This is exactly the kv_prefix_sharing issue. We should avoid sharing prefix buffers across websocket streams by default for quant canaries.

oncall-sre: created alert rule staging/parse_noise_high: structured-output-parse-rate > 0.2% for 5m. alert_id=ALRT-1730

sam: created a short kernel bench that measures per-token latency jitter across fp16 vs int8 with identical prompts. initial run shows median same but 95p jitter increased ~12ms on int8 for these prompts. spike could cause micro-batch boundary misalignment.

leo: i can flip canary to isolated prefix pools (isolate_prefix=true) and re-run. will schedule.

tanya: for the SDK repair step, keep it opt-in and emit a trace when repair applied (so we can avoid hiding regressions). repair heuristic: if parse fails and last token looks like an open bracket/brace, append matching closer(s) and reparse once. log original and repaired payloads.

sam: also add unit test that simulates half-token flush: random split inside UTF-8 multi-byte sequence to ensure we handle byte-level fragmentation.

leo: isolating prefixes now. runtime-bot: deploy 1730000078 by leo: isolate_prefix=true for kestrel-lite-int8 canary. status=success

leo: re-run results: failures down to 0.02% on 5k replay. pushing the harness to CI.

oncall-sre: thanks. i've added a forwarding rule to persist raw token streams for 1h for failing requests to storage/sandbox for bisecting.

tanya: next steps: (A) upstream kernel team to investigate int8 emission jitter (sam), (B) keep repair-step opt-in and collect telemetry (leo), (C) consider disabling kv_prefix_sharing for websocket streaming by default in canary mode (ops ticket).

leo: ack. will open PRs for repair-step and test harness, and follow up after next replay (~30m).
